answer: Rate limiting at the karst: each identity maps to a subnet fingerprint, capping new IDs at 3 per /24 per epoch. The voyage across ASNs costs attackers fresh IP ranges; fingerprinting makes reuse detectable. A whisper of collusion triggers a 10x fee multiplier. Scaling to 1,000 sybils needs ~334 distinct subnets, raising cost from $50 to $16,700. The mechanism works because per-subnet throttling forces linear capital expenditure against linear returns, breaking farm economics.
